Atomic requirement: Every claim shall reference one or more evidence records
Source basis: EPA DQO information-input and acceptance-criteria concepts

Atomic requirement: A claim shall not be promoted above the weakest supporting evidence component
A measurement shall not be treated as verified when its calibration is expired, absent, or inapplicable
Each completed boundary shall include upstream, downstream, mechanism, variable, method, provenance, uncertainty, and reviewer
The ledger shall reject personal identifiers, device identifiers, biometrics, health data, raw audio, imagery, and movement history
The evidence workflow shall remain read-only and shall not generate equipment-control instructions
Incompatible evidence shall preserve both records and emit a review-required conflict
Separation evidence shall not be represented as destruction without disposition evidence
Public-facing output shall identify uncertainty, limits, review status, and accessible review paths
Every AI-assisted output shall be traceable to source artifacts, transformations, uncertainty state, and review owner
